reference_on: Preserve the exact lettering content, glyph silhouettes, small kana, dakuten and punctuation in <Picture 1>. Keep the established lettering style and arrangement. Modify only the requested decoration; do not redesign or replace the glyphs. If a new writing direction is explicitly requested, reflow the same readable characters into that direction.
reference_off: Create the lettering from the text instruction alone.
horizontal: Arrange the lettering horizontally, read from left to right. Follow explicit line breaks. Give individual characters lively spacing and slight expressive tilts while keeping the complete text readable.
vertical: Arrange the lettering in exactly {rows} rows in one narrow upright column. Read each row once from top to bottom in this exact order: {units}. Each Japanese character stays upright, not rotated sideways. Keep small kana noticeably smaller. A final punctuation group occupies one shared row below the last kana, with its marks side by side.

Use thick, rounded, bouncy Japanese display lettering with lively spacing, clear counters and playful individual tilts. Keep every character upright and recognizable. No surrounding symbols or extra text. DETACHED DAKUTEN: For every voiced kana such as ビ, make three disconnected black shapes: the kana body and two separate short dakuten strokes. Place BOTH dakuten entirely ABOVE the body. The bottom of EACH dakuten must be higher than the highest edge of the kana body. Leave a wide pure-white gap beneath both dakuten, at least one complete dakuten height, and a clear white gap between the two dakuten. The main kana upper arm ends well below the floating marks. Never attach, bridge, fuse or overlap either dakuten with the kana body. Do not turn dakuten into circles or punctuation.

dakuten_priority: PRIORITY: Make every dakuten visibly detached. Shift both short dakuten marks farther UP and RIGHT than standard typesetting, so their complete bounding boxes lie above and to the right of the main kana body. Leave a broad band of pure white between the body and both marks. Think of one lower base glyph plus two separately floating accents, never a connected font outline. Preserve the exact requested voiced kana and its two marks.
